title: אביי הכהן

paragraphs: Abaye the priest. (1) His name was Nachmani, after his grandfather, Rabbah’s father. Shabbat 33, end of a: “I know Nachmani”; there, 74a, Rava says, “Nachmani has spoken well”; likewise Me'ilah 20b, Rava says, “Nachmani has spoken well.” Avodah Zarah, chapter Rabbi Yishmael: Rava says, “Nachmani has surrounded us with teachings.” Chapter Hashole'ach: the anonymous Gemara says, “The law follows Nachmani.” Gittin 45a: he lost a donkey among the Kutim and gave the identifying mark that its belly was white. They sent him, “Were you not Nachmani”—meaning that he does not lie—etc. The Arukh, entry Abaye, likewise writes: “His name was Nachmani; he was the nephew and student of Rabbah bar Nachmani. Since his name was Nachmani, after Rabbah’s father, Rabbah did not constantly call him Nachmani by his father’s name, but called him Abaye in Aramaic, like someone saying ‘my father’; thus Abaye became his name.” End quotation. Rashi, chapter Hamekabbel, likewise: he called him Abaye to avoid calling him by his father’s name. Some explain the reverse: his name was Abaye, and Rabbah, who raised him and taught him Torah, called him Nachmani after his father, since he was like a son to him. Rashi likewise explains in Gittin 34b. As for Rashi, end of Horayot, “Some say he called him Nachmani disparagingly, meaning you are still Rav Nachman’s student”: Be'er Sheva writes that this is an error, written by a mistaken student [ותלמוד טועה כתבו; the printed wording is irregular]. (Certainly an error, for I cited above the anonymous Gemara’s ruling “The law follows Nachmani.” Moreover, Pesachim 112b: he decreed that Igrat daughter of Machalat should not enter settled places. She told him, “Had they not proclaimed in heaven, ‘Beware of Nachmani,’ I would have endangered you.” In chapter Af Al Pi, Choma came before Rava after Abaye’s death and said, “Allot me wine.” He said, “I know that Nachmani did not drink wine.” If Nachmani were disparaging, the anonymous Gemara, heaven, and those speaking after his death would not call him Nachmani; this is clear.) His father died before he was born, and his mother died after his birth. They said that Abaye is an acronym of “For in You an orphan will find mercy” [אשר בך ירוחם יתום] (Hosea 14:2). Megalleh Amukkot, no. 92 [א׳ צ״ב]: “Only against me does He turn again” [אך בי ישוב יהפך] (Lamentations 3), fulfilling “You have been the orphan’s helper.” Abaye’s statements “Mother told me,” Shabbat 66b, 134a; Eruvin 29b, 65a; Yoma 78b; Mo'ed Katan 12a, 18b, refer to his foster mother (Kiddushin 31b).

(2) He was of the house of Eli, and his father was called Kaylil. Zevachim 118b: when Abaye raised an objection to Rav Yosef, he told him, “Kaylil had one son, and he does not conduct himself properly” (see there). In chapter Hazzeroa, 133a, he accepted priestly gifts only on the eve of Yom Kippur, so people would know he was a priest. (Tosafot there: he was not wealthy. Eruvin 65a: Rabbah bar Rav Chanan came to Abaye and asked, “You and Rabbah did not have an eruv?” It appears he was not wealthy enough to provide the eruv from his own property.) He did not pronounce the priestly blessing because the students studied with him at the time of raising the hands: Rashi and the Arukh, entry adan. (Its wording: they did not allow him to get up, since they were studying.) Rosh writes that he had an intestinal illness and could not spread his hands.

(3) A greeting came to him from the heavenly academy every eve of Shabbat (see above, Abba the bloodletter). When a Torah scholar finished a tractate he would make a festive day for them, Shabbat 118, end of b. He slept during the day for the time it takes to walk six parasangs; Rav Yosef applied to him, “How long, lazy man, will you lie down?”, Sukkah 26b. When he wished to have intercourse, he drove away the flies [following Rashi’s explanation of באלי דידבי], Niddah 17. In his old age he married Choma, daughter of Issi, son of Rabbi Yitzchak, son of Rav Yehudah. She was beautiful (Ketubbot 65a) and had already been widowed from two husbands, great sages: first Rachava of Pumbedita, then Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbah bar bar Chana. Abaye held that the law did not follow Rabbi, who says that two occurrences establish a presumption (Yevamot 64b). He married her and soon died. He occupied himself with Torah and acts of kindness and lived sixty years, Rosh Hashanah 18; Yevamot 105a. He had academies in Rav Yosef’s lifetime (see below, Rava). See part I, year 4099, as to when he became academy head and when he died. Some say he headed it thirteen years, others fourteen. As children Abaye and Rava were before Rabbah, who called them “gourds, gourds,” Berakhot 48a; see there. Abaye performed before Rava (it should read Rabbah, as in Ein Yaakov) with eight eggs; some say four, throwing one and catching one, Sukkah 53a. Abaye gave his hand to an elder, Kiddushin 33, end of a; see Rashi’s two explanations. Rav Acha Gaon, of blessed memory (She'iltot of Rabbi Acha of Shabcha, Kedoshim), writes: “One who does not rise before the rabbis is compelled to rise, to honor the Torah. When Abaye passed and elders could not rise, he gave them a hand and they rose. Rava sent an emissary ahead to make the public rise. Rav Nachman sent attendants; upon arriving he told them, ‘Were it not for Torah, how many Nachmans are in the marketplace! When you rise, you rise before Torah, not before me.’” End quotation. (See below, Rav Nachman.) That is, sages are obliged, for the Torah’s honor, to compel people to rise before them. (See above, Rabbi Abba the priest bar Pappa.) Abaye supports the elders with his hand so they may rise before Abaye; Rav Pappa on his right and Rav Huna son of Rabbi Yehoshua on his left. End of Yuchasin. (There is a scribal error and an omission here: “so they may rise before Abaye” ends Rav Acha Gaon’s words. Then it should continue: Pesachim 111 says Abaye saw Ketev Meriri approaching and placed Rav Pappa on his right and Rav Huna bar Yehoshua on his left—meaning on Ketev Meriri’s side, since his time was favorable.) Yevamot 122, beginning of a: the woman who came before Abaye, whom he delayed three festivals. (Rashi: scholars gathered to hear the laws of Passover. In the Geonim’s name: when a great man dies, each year they appoint that day in his honor, and scholars gather at his grave to hold an academy there; see Rav Adda bar Ahavah.) Kiddushin 29: a harmful being with seven heads was in Abaye’s academy, harming entrants even by day. Hearing that Rav Acha bar Yaakov was coming (see there), Abaye said no one should give him lodging, so he would stay in the academy; perhaps a miracle would occur. He stayed there, and with every bow as he prayed concerning the harmful being, one head fell off. (Gilgulei Neshamot, letter alef, writes: “Abaye was the old man who took the concubine at Gibeah into his house; Rabbi Acha bar Yaakov was the concubine’s husband, and the serpent was the concubine. Because the incident occurred in his house, this harmful being now inhabited Abaye’s academy to avenge itself on the rabbis, reincarnations of the people of Gibeah who committed the outrage all night. Abaye understood but could not repair it, because the initial corruption was in his house: had he not taken her in, it would not have occurred thus. Therefore he said no one should give him lodging; perhaps he has an affinity and connection to his concubine and would stay there. So it was. Retribution is exacted from the effect as from the cause: now all were punished and repaired, since Rav Acha experienced great fear. The seven-headed serpent signifies how many thousands and myriads of Israel fell then.” End quotation.) On the seven heads see Rav Acha bar Yaakov. When joyful he said, “I am like Ben Azzai in the markets of Tiberias,” Kiddushin 20a; Sotah 45, end of a. Arakhin 30, beginning of b, Rashi explains: “I am distinguished in my place, an expositor and expert like Ben Azzai.” On Rava’s identical saying in Eruvin 29a Rashi explains: “Ready to answer sharply,” etc. Since the end of Horayot expressly implies Abaye was more of a ‘Sinai’ than Rava, Rashi did not explain Rava as boasting of expertise—Abaye had more—but of sharpness (see below, Rava was sharper). So Be'er Sheva writes at the end of Horayot. Responsa Chut Hashani 23b writes that he overlooked two explicit passages: the same Arakhin passage occurs in Kiddushin 20a and Sotah, chapter 9,45a, where Abaye too says, “I am like Ben Azzai.” In both places Rashi explains as for Rava in Eruvin. Thus Be'er Sheva’s explanation cannot stand; see there. Responsa Ralbach writes: in “All Israel’s sages are before me like a garlic peel,” “before me” is an error and should read “seem to me,” as the reading in Bekhorot concerning Ben Azzai.

(4) His teacher was Rabbah bar Nachmani the priest. (Zevachim 34b: “He asked Rava” should read Rabbah, as in the new Talmud editions [שס״ח].) Rav Yosef was his colleague, though Kiddushin 33a says that when Abaye saw the ears of Rav Yosef’s approaching donkey he rose. It appears Rav Yosef was also Abaye’s teacher. (See Menachot 35b: Abaye sat before Rav Yosef; see the rules I wrote, that “sat before” indicates a student.) But Abaye appears to have been Rav Yosef’s student-colleague: at the end of Yotze Dofen he asked Rav Yosef, “Do you disagree?”, not “Does the master disagree?” (Likewise Arakhin, end of chapter 4.) Shabbat 45b: Abaye told Rav Yosef, “And do you not hold so?” Chapter Ha'ishah: “You told us” (see Rav Yosef), as they deduced that Rabbi Yirmeyah was Rav’s student-colleague (see there). Moreover, in the rulings on Eruvin, R.M. writes that the law follows Abaye against Rav Yosef except concerning ‘half,’ the one ruling in the first chapter of Eruvin where the law follows Rav Yosef against Abaye. He raised a contradiction to Rav Yosef (Shabbat 46b), and called his colleague Rava “master” and asked Rava (see there). Rav Yosef was academy head; after his death Abaye headed it, and afterward Rava: end of Hannizakin, end of Berakhot, end of Horayot. When Abaye was appointed, Rabbi Zeira, Rabbah bar Mattanah, and Rava were with him. All were refuted, while he was not; he became head. Rava told him, “Begin, Nachmani.” [The retrieved Horayot text names Rabbah here.] Yuchasin writes that when Ulla came to Pumbedita, Abaye was with Rav Chisda and his son Rav Yitzchak. (See the confused wording and omission here: Pesachim 104b says that when Ulla came to Pumbedita, Rav Yehudah told his son Rabbi Yitzchak to observe Ulla’s havdalah. He did not go, and sent Abaye. For what requires examination see Ulla.) When Rav Huna died Abaye was with Rabbah and Rav Chisda. Rav Dimi called him ‘skull-man.’ He did not see Rabbi Yochanan (see there). Chullin 77a: a broken bone protruded, and its fragment was removed. It came before Abaye, who delayed it three festivals. Rav Adda bar Mattanah told the animal’s owner, “Go to Rava, whose knife is sharp.” Rav Adda bar Ahavah [the retrieved Bava Batra text names Rav Adda bar Abba] was punished for saying, “Instead of gnawing bones” (the Arukh reads “grinding bones”) “at Abaye’s, eat meat at Rava’s.” Chiddushei Aggadot writes that ‘bones,’ גרמי, has the numerical value of יע״ל קג״ם, the cases where the law alone follows Abaye (see Rava): yod, despair without knowledge (Bava Metzia 22); ayin, a conspiring witness (Sanhedrin, printed יכ״ז); lamed, a side-post standing of itself (Eruvin 15a); qof, betrothals not permitting intercourse (Kiddushin 51); gimel, disclosure of intention in divorce (Gittin 34); mem, an apostate (Sanhedrin 27). Tosafot, Niddah 37a, identify the lamed of יע״ל with days of childbirth. See Semag, Laws of Niddah, section 111; Tosafot, Kiddushin 52a; Yam Shel Shelomo, Bava Kamma, chapter 7, section 103; Shabbat 155a. Where something is clear to Abaye but a question to Rava, we follow Abaye (Milchamot Hashem, Bava Kamma 10a).

(5) Abaye is of Cain’s mystery, and therefore the law did not follow him, etc. He maintained Ben Azzai’s way (see below, Shammai), drawing converts’ souls through Torah: Abaye’s nefesh, ruach, and neshamah were of Cain’s mystery, all of the nefesh aspect on the side of Malkhut. Therefore he was an orphan who saw neither father nor mother and repaired converts’ souls, which have no father or mother. When joyful he said, “I am like Ben Azzai,” as above: through joy he drew converts’ souls (Chesed LeAvraham, spring 5, stream 25). He came from Eli, who was a reincarnation of Yael; they were from the root קיץ [kayitz, literally ‘summer’; comparison with the Cain/Eli/Yael passages suggests Cain, but the Hebrew reading is retained] (Sefer Hakkavvanot, miscellanies, Judges). He was a reincarnation of Yotam son of Uzziah, called Yerucham (see part I, year 3167). See above: אשר בך ירוחם יתום, the initials Abaye, hinting that he was Yerucham’s reincarnation. See Likkutei Ha'ari: אהל בל יצען יתדותיו, the initials Abaye. Reversed, it is Yeyva: he was Rabbi Yeyva the elder’s reincarnation, his name reversed from Yeyva to Abaye. בל יצען בל יסע gives the initials Bibi, hinting at his son Rav Bibi. (G.A.Y. writes: Baniom is a cave of Dimyaos; Abaye and Rava are buried in the cave. See Rabbi Yose ben Kisma.)

(6) Abba the bloodletter in his time; before Rabbi Abba (Me'ilah 3b), and Rabbi Abba told him, Chullin 97b. Abba bar Avin; Abba bar Marta asked him; Abba bar Chanan called him ‘tarda’ [תרדא; Rashi explains “fool,” alternatively “idler”; the speaker’s name differs between witnesses]. Rabbi Avin called him “master,” and Abaye called him “Avin the bereaved.” He spoke to Rav Adda of Naresh. Rabbi Adda bar Marta before him, and asked him; he spoke to Rav Avya. Rav Acha bar Ulla in his name; Rav Acha bar Huna; Rav Acha bar Minyomi spoke to him; Rav Acha. Rav Acha Salla the great in his name (so Yuchasin; name not found). Rav Acha Salla, grandson of Rabbi Acha Salla the great, said in Abaye’s name (so Yuchasin; see there; it is an error). Rav Acha bar Yaakov (see above); Rav Acha bar Pinchas. Rav Acha bar Ika’s father spoke to Abaye. Rav Acha bar Tachlifa spoke to him. Rav Idi bar Avin the carpenter sent before him. Rav Ika bar Avin (see there); Rav Ika, Rabbi Acha’s father; Rabbi Alexander. He spoke to Rabbi Ilai; explained Rabbi Ammi bar Tuvya’s words. Rav Bibi, his son. He spoke to Rav Dimi; Rav Dimi bar Yosef spoke to him. He permitted for Rav Dimi bar Lua. He challenged bar Hedya; bar Hedya interpreted his dream. Havu [הבו; relation unresolved]. Rav Huna bar Chinena; Rav Huna bar Idi, his student; Rav Huna bar Moshe bar Atzar; Hillel son of Rabbi Yehudah Nesia in his time (so Yuchasin; I did not find it). Rav Zevid in his name; Rabbi Zevida; Rabbi Zeira; Rabbi Zerika. He spoke to Rav Ze'ira. Bar Chavu; he spoke to Rabbi Chagga. Chizkiyah in his name; Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, his student; Rabbi Chiyya bar Minyomi. He heard what Rabbi Chiyya bar Ammi said. He said in Rabbi Chama bar Ukva’s name; Rabbi Chanina bar Minyomi spoke to him; he asked Rav Chisda. Abaye—another reading, Rav Sheshet—spoke to Rav Chisda’s interpreter. He asked Rav Chananel (the early Abaye). Rav Chanina bar Avin; Rav Tuvya bar Rav Tavyomi in his name. Mar Yehudah spoke to him. Rav Yehudah in his name (requires examination; perhaps the early Abaye). Rabbi Yonah in his name; Rav Yosef, his teacher; Rabbi Yaakov bar Abba, his student; Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha bar Yaakov and his father studied before him; Rabbi Yaakov bar Tachlifa, his student; Rabbi Yitzchak bar Abba; Rabbi Yitzchak bar Rav Yehudah (see above). Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef called him “master”; Rabbi Yishmael bar Yosef; “master”—he told him several things. Mar Kashisha bar Rav Chisda spoke to him. Rabbah sent him to Mari bar Mar; Rav Mordekhai asked him. Rav Mari bar Rav Shmuel bar Shilat in his name; Rav Mari son of Mar Shmuel said in Abaye’s name; Rav Mesharshya, Rava’s son, his student. Rav Mattanah spoke to him. Rav Nachumi bar Zekharyah asked him. In Rav Nachman’s name (Eruvin 3b); Be'er Sheva, Horayot: Rav Nachman was Abaye’s teacher. Rav Nachman bar Minyomi; Rav Natan bar Hoshaya. Rav Safra objected to him; Ulla. Ulla bar Rav asked him; Rav Ulla bar Ashi asked him; Rabbi Ila. He spoke to Rav Amram; Rav Pappa, his student. He said in Rav’s name (Bava Batra 167b); explained Rav’s words (Shabbat 57, end of b)—requires examination; perhaps the early Abaye. His colleague Rava bar Chanan spoke to him; Rava, his colleague; Rava bar bar Chana. Rava bar Sharshom and his father before him; Rava bar Lima challenged him. He spoke to Rava bar Azza; Rabbah bar bar Chana spoke to him. Rabbah, his teacher; Rabbah bar Chanan bar Abba, his colleague. He spoke to Rabbah bar Chanina. Ravin appears to be his student. Ravnai in his name. He spoke to Rachava; Rav Rechumi spoke to him; ben Rechumi asked him. He said in Resh Lakish’s name; spoke to Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yehudah. Rav Shmuel bar Bisna asked him; Rav Sherevya spoke to him.
